lane: Adjacent testing, profiling and runtime diagnostics
method: Read the 89-profile inventory, searched all authored docs for coverage/profiling/mutation/load terminology, and inspected existing generated-testing, runtime and API profiles.
Read content and builder schemas to distinguish additive catalog vocabulary from evidence needed for automated matching.
Checked only official project/vendor documentation and repository license files for proposed capabilities, setup, outputs and limitations.
No browser interaction, installations, analyzer/example execution, product edits or performance measurements.
summary: Four bounded candidates add execution coverage, mutation testing, Python sampling and HTTP load testing. These are expansion opportunities, not defects in the existing scoped catalog. Prioritize foundation/example improvements and existing-domain gaps before admitting all four.

coverage_matrix.current: Coverage-guided fuzzers use execution feedback, and profiles repeatedly qualify exercised behavior. There is no dedicated line/branch coverage measurement profile.
coverage_matrix.gap: Which application lines/branches did an existing test run exercise?
coverage_matrix.scope: One Python test suite, explicit source scope and statement/branch report.

coverage_matrix.current: Hypothesis and fast-check generate inputs for user-supplied properties. Mutation-based fuzzing is present, but no source-mutation test-quality workflow is documented.
coverage_matrix.gap: Do existing assertions detect selected injected changes to program behavior?
coverage_matrix.scope: One JavaScript project with the documented Jest runner; other languages/runners require separate review.

coverage_matrix.current: Memory/race tools detect selected correctness problems; Staticcheck explicitly says its performance-related diagnostics are not runtime measurements.
coverage_matrix.gap: Where does a Python process spend sampled execution time under a chosen workload?
coverage_matrix.scope: Local CPython stack sampling; exclude native-extension, container and remote deployment claims from first admission.

coverage_matrix.current: Schemathesis and RESTler focus on generated requests, response/specification violations and configured failures; no load-testing profile or latency/throughput finding category exists.
coverage_matrix.gap: Does a test endpoint meet stated response-time/error thresholds under a defined load?
coverage_matrix.scope: Local CLI HTTP scenario with an explicit workload and thresholds; exclude cloud, browser and distributed execution from first admission.

findings.title: Add an execution-coverage workflow before treating test reach as understood
findings.reader_task: Find unexecuted Python lines and branches in an existing test run.
findings.evidence: The inventory contains coverage-guided fuzzers but no coverage-measurement profile or test-coverage finding category. The generated-tests concept explains failure detectors without a separate route for measuring which code an existing suite exercised. Fuzzer guidance does not substitute for a coverage report over a chosen test suite.
findings.impact: A reader can choose input generators but lacks a direct path to inspect test reach and its denominator.
findings.confidence: High for the local coverage gap; prioritization is reviewer judgment.
findings.recommendation: Add coverage.py as a scoped Python execution-coverage profile and link it from Hypothesis and the generated-tests concept. Start with an existing small test suite, declared source scope and branch measurement. Include a short explanation of execution coverage versus assertion strength.

candidate.name: coverage.py
candidate.admission_readiness: Primary documentation supports a catalog profile. Pin a package release and matching Python/runtime requirements when authoring; no execution verified.
candidate.purpose_input: Python code exercised through an existing test runner or program invocation, with configured source selection.
candidate.setup: Install the official coverage package into the selected environment; run the test command under coverage with branch collection, then produce text/HTML or machine-readable reports.
candidate.findings: Reports measured and missing lines/branches. Source/include/omit settings change the measured denominator.
candidate.limitations: Branch coverage and statement coverage differ. Subprocesses need deliberate collection/combination. Process termination can prevent data from being written. Our interpretation: execution alone does not establish that assertions are adequate or behavior is correct.
candidate.license: Apache-2.0 except where otherwise noted, per the project's NOTICE.txt.
candidate.overlap: Complements Hypothesis and ordinary test suites; it does not replace the failure oracle or provide automatic bug discovery.
candidate.unresolved: No runtime/environment combination was exercised. Keep advanced concurrency/process modes outside the initial single-process recipe.

sources.supports: Official supported runtimes, installation and test-runner invocation/reporting.
Branch measurement and report meaning.
Source selection and omitted/unexecuted files affect reported scope.
Process startup, termination and combination requirements.
Apache-2.0 qualification.

acceptance: Reader can identify the measured source scope, an unexecuted line and a missing branch in illustrative output.
The example distinguishes full line coverage from full branch coverage and from effective assertions.
State whether data covers one process or a configured process tree, and whether the run completed.
Link a single reusable test fixture/run record; retain an unexecuted label until later hands-on validation.
Add a precise coverage-measurement technique/result label without relabeling existing fuzzers as coverage-report tools.
dependencies: Reusable test fixture and run-record guidance
findings.compatibility: Finding and technique values are extensible strings, so a scoped catalog entry need not migrate existing data. Source/test execution preparation must be explicit. Existing harness/testInstance access flags express broad preparation, but runner/version/scope evidence still needs review before adding a builder workflow; catalog-only admission is acceptable.

findings.title: Separate mutation testing from input mutation and coverage counts
findings.reader_task: Evaluate whether an existing JavaScript test suite detects selected source-code changes.
findings.evidence: The catalog has property-based input generation and a Mutation-based fuzzing technique, but no mutation-testing profile. The concept comparison does not distinguish changing test inputs from injecting changes into application code and rerunning its tests.
findings.impact: Readers lack a way to investigate assertion sensitivity and may confuse two workflows that both use the word mutation.
findings.confidence: High for the local gap; no comparative effectiveness benchmark performed.
findings.recommendation: Pilot StrykerJS on one JavaScript/Jest project with an already working suite. Add a concise distinction between execution coverage, source mutation and input mutation. Keep other runners and TypeScript-specific handling outside the first workflow until reviewed.

candidate.name: StrykerJS
candidate.admission_readiness: Ready for a narrowly scoped documentation-led profile after selecting compatible Stryker/Node/Jest versions. Initial scope is JavaScript with the official Jest runner.
candidate.purpose_input: Selected application source files and their existing tests/configuration.
candidate.setup: Use official initializer/configuration guidance, install the matching runner, define mutation scope and confirm the initial test run. Retain default temporary-copy execution rather than introducing in-place mutation in a first example.
candidate.findings: Reports killed, survived, uncovered, timed-out, erroneous or ignored mutants and a score derived from the tool's status rules.
candidate.limitations: Equivalent mutants can survive without representing a missing behavioral test. Exclusions, selected operators, test setup and timeouts affect interpretation. Runtime or compile errors are not equivalent to killed mutants.
candidate.overlap: Complements fast-check and existing tests by assessing their response to selected code mutations; it is not input fuzzing, compiler type checking or a proof of test completeness.
candidate.unresolved: No integration executed. Broader runner/framework compatibility and TypeScript checker behavior require separate scoped evidence.

sources.supports: Initializer, configuration and invocation.
Official Jest runner installation and integration.
Mutation scope, dry run, temporary sandbox, report choices and excluded files.
Distinct mutant statuses and metric interpretation.
Survival does not always mean an observable behavior difference can be asserted.
Apache-2.0 license.

acceptance: Explain source mutation separately from changing fuzz inputs.
The first workflow uses an explicit small source subset and a working test runner.
Show how one meaningful surviving mutation can motivate a stronger assertion without demanding an arbitrary score of 100%.
Explain the treatment of errors/timeouts/exclusions and equivalent mutants.
Record tool, runner, target revision and mutation configuration; do not claim an illustrative run occurred.
findings.compatibility: A new Mutation testing technique and carefully worded test-sensitivity result category are additive. Do not reuse Mutation-based fuzzing as if equivalent. Existing source/callable inputs and harness/testInstance requirements can express broad preparation, but use catalog-only admission until the chosen runner workflow is independently scoped; preserve v1 imports.

findings.title: Add a scoped Python runtime-profiling path
findings.reader_task: Investigate sampled hot paths in a local Python workload.
findings.evidence: No profile has a profiling technique or runtime-performance result category. Staticcheck correctly distinguishes its code-pattern findings from actual latency/profiling; memory and race entries answer different questions.
findings.impact: The wiki has a clear correctness-analysis boundary but no next step for investigating observed runtime cost.
findings.confidence: High for local absence; no overhead or accuracy measurements performed.
findings.recommendation: Add py-spy for local CPython sampling, with a launch-under-profiler route as the first documented path. Explain the chosen sampling window/workload and how to investigate a hot path. Avoid a blanket production-safety or zero-overhead claim.

candidate.name: py-spy
candidate.admission_readiness: Official documentation supports a local CPython profile. Select a release/host/interpreter combination during authoring; no execution verified.
candidate.purpose_input: A local CPython process or a command launched under the sampler.
candidate.setup: Install the project release and record a reproducible workload to a flame graph or profile file. Attach permissions depend on host and process relationship.
candidate.findings: Sampled Python stacks, live function summaries, or a thread-stack snapshot.
candidate.limitations: Sampling and idle/GIL filtering affect interpretation. Native-extension support is platform-specific; omit it from first scope. Inference: sampled hot paths do not establish correctness or a complete execution trace.
candidate.overlap: Complements correctness checkers; it does not replace memory/race detection or controlled load testing.
candidate.unresolved: No compatibility or overhead measured. Container, native-extension and production-attachment workflows remain outside initial scope.

sources.supports: Official README: install, record/top/dump, host/CPython support, attach permissions and sampling qualifications.
MIT license.

acceptance: Profile explains what a sampled stack means for the selected workload and interval.
Installation/setup link identifies release-specific interpreter/host scope.
Permission/setup failure is distinguished from successful recording.
Native, container and production claims are absent unless separately supported.
Label all sample profiles illustrative unless execution evidence is later retained.
findings.compatibility: Running applications can describe the artifact, but current builder access flags do not explicitly capture process inspection/attach permission. Begin catalog-only rather than marking all Python processes ready. Any later access-model extension must preserve existing v1 descriptions and default absent access information to unknown.

findings.title: Add HTTP load testing with explicit workload and threshold semantics
findings.reader_task: Check a test service against stated latency/error goals under a defined workload.
findings.evidence: Current API tools emphasize schema/stateful input generation and configured failures. The inventory has no dedicated load-testing entry or latency/throughput result category, so existing HTTP scope does not answer the performance question.
findings.impact: Readers seeking API reliability/performance have no route that distinguishes service behavior under chosen demand from functional/security checks.
findings.confidence: High for the gap; no load tests or service-capacity measurements performed.
findings.recommendation: Add a local Grafana k6 OSS HTTP workflow and link it as complementary to Schemathesis/RESTler. Start with a disposable endpoint, a stated load model, a short bounded test and explicit thresholds; keep cloud, distributed and browser paths outside the first profile.

candidate.name: Grafana k6 OSS
candidate.admission_readiness: Official docs support local HTTP CLI use. Pin the selected release and script semantics before authoring; this review did not execute a load.
candidate.purpose_input: A reachable test HTTP service and a user-authored workload script.
candidate.setup: Install the local k6 CLI, prepare test data/authentication/reset behavior and define scenario duration/load plus thresholds. The local run does not require choosing the cloud execution product.
candidate.findings: Request/error and timing measurements, plus pass/fail outcomes against configured metric thresholds.
candidate.limitations: Boolean checks alone do not fail the whole test; thresholds provide failure criteria. Closed and open workload models produce different arrival behavior. Inference: measured results describe the workload/environment, not universal capacity or security.
candidate.license: AGPL-3.0 license text for the open-source k6 repository; cloud service terms are outside this profile.
candidate.overlap: Complements schema fuzzing and security testing. JavaScript used for the driver does not restrict the target's implementation language.
candidate.unresolved: No host/network/load-generator adequacy or endpoint behavior was benchmarked. Browser, cloud, distributed execution and extensions require separate reviews.

sources.supports: Official local CLI installation paths.
Local runs, virtual users, duration and execution-mode separation.
Measurements and metric types.
Configured metric criteria and failed test status.
A failed check does not itself give the entire test a failed status.
Arrival model and response-time coupling limitations.
AGPL version 3 license text.

acceptance: Reader can identify the endpoint, test-data/reset assumptions, workload, duration and pass/fail criteria.
Explain check versus threshold behavior and distinguish missing/failed setup from a passed measurement.
Record target revision/environment and load-generator conditions without claiming results transfer unchanged to production.
Comparison with Schemathesis/RESTler explains different questions rather than ranking generic API coverage.
Initial example uses a local disposable service or clearly bounded official tutorial, labeled unexecuted until validated.
dependencies: Reusable API fixture/reset instructions from REX-02
findings.compatibility: An HTTP connection workflow can use existing Running applications, HTTP API, harness and testInstance fields, with a reviewed threshold-specific result category. Keep target language independent. New optional catalog labels do not require changing v1 files; do not add browser/cloud/other protocol matches from the aggregate product scope.

ordering_rationale: Execution measurement and assertion sensitivity deepen the existing generated-testing explanation; sampling and load tests then extend runtime diagnosis. All remain later expansion work after concrete navigation, authoring and recipe fixes.

deferred_categories.reason: The first need is reusable test fixtures and interpretation, not a broad framework directory. Existing Hypothesis/fast-check docs can link compatible runners.
Instrumentation, data pipelines and service topology would broaden setup substantially; no bounded candidate selected in this pass.
One documented entry per missing question establishes the decision model before comparison breadth.
Useful adjacent area, but not selected ahead of the four gaps and existing frontend-audit findings.

limits: Catalog absence is not proof that no existing product offers an undocumented ancillary capability.
Recommended labels and builder boundaries are proposals; no metadata/schema changes were made.
Current official docs were read as of 2026-11-06. Moving latest/master links should be pinned to the chosen release when authoring version-specific examples.
The unreachable coverage.py license.html route was replaced by the official repository NOTICE.txt; no candidate license depends on that failed lookup.
No benchmark, production-safety certification or measured compatibility claim is made.
